title: Inside the fish (Jonah 2)
hookLine: three days in the dark, Jonah prays from the belly

lines: WHAT DOES HE DO IN THERE?
cards: The sailors let go, and the sea closes over his head. Seaweed. Cold.
The last light going green, then gone. Then, in the King James Bible, a short, flat sentence: "Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah." Notice prepared.
The fish isn't an accident, or a punishment out of nowhere. It was ready. And the story doesn't describe the inside of the fish at all.
No ribs, no stomach, no smell. It skips straight to what Jonah does in there.

teach.b: He prays. "Then Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish's belly." Up to now, Jonah has done everything except pray.
He slept while the sailors prayed; the captain had to shake him awake.

teach.h: A PSALM FROM THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA.
teach.b: Now, at the very bottom, three days and three nights in the dark, the words finally come. The prayer is shaped like a psalm, its lines echoing the Psalms, as if he reached for prayers he already knew.
He describes drowning: waters closing in, weeds wrapped around his head, going down to the roots of the mountains. And: "out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice."
Hell there is the King James word for Sheol, the place of the dead. He feels as far from God as a person can get.
Yet the prayer ends in thanks, while he's still inside the fish, before anything has changed. Its last line is short: "Salvation is of the LORD." Then the fish spits him out onto dry land.
One more thing: the book of Jonah never calls it a whale.
The Hebrew says a great fish. The whale came later, in some translations of Jesus's words in Matthew, where he points to Jonah's three days in the dark as a sign of his own three days in the grave.
Some Christians hear Jonah's prayer as Easter in miniature: someone given up for lost, praying from the bottom, and brought back up.

how: Christians read Jonah 2 alongside Jesus's words about the sign of Jonah in Matthew 12, and some hear Jonah's three days in the fish as a picture of the resurrection.

o: the creature God prepared, never called a whale
a sea monster sent to punish the prophet
a whale, the word the book of Jonah uses

games.q: what's inside Jonah 2 — tap the pairs.
p: Sheol, the place of the dead
Jesus's three days in the grave

s: the book of Jonah says a whale swallowed him
the Hebrew says a great fish. the whale came later, in some translations of Matthew.
Jonah gives thanks while still inside the fish
the prayer ends in thanks, before he's back on dry land.
the story describes the inside of the fish in detail
it skips the inside completely and goes straight to Jonah's prayer.

games.q: you're Jonah, three days in the dark inside a great fish. you ran from God, and now you can't run anywhere. what do you do?
o: pray, and give thanks before anything changes.
promise to pray once you're out.
games.why: he prays from the fish's belly, and the prayer ends in thanks: "salvation is of the LORD." then the fish spits him onto dry land.

practice: Jonah didn't wait to be out of the fish or tidy up first; he prayed from the dark, weeds around his head.
So, wherever you are, on a bus, in bed, in a hard week, name plainly how things are right now, then find one thing to be grateful for before anything changes.
If you pray, speak to God from exactly this spot; if not, say the honest words to yourself and let them be heard.

wordCard.voice: Great fish. What the book of Jonah actually calls the creature that swallowed him, prepared and ready, never once called a whale.
